extracted.intended_audience: investigative journalists, journalism trainers, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and evaluating investigative journalism, emphasizing follow-the-money techniques. Covers core story criteria, step-by-step financial-tracing methods, recommended training topics, and newsworthiness factors for investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts not previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should produce new information or revelations rather than rehashing existing reporting; demonstrates reporter initiative and adds to public knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters affecting many people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should concern issues with broad public impact or importance, not merely private disputes or niche topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporter’s own work, not handed by sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporter must drive the reporting process (sourcing, verification, analysis) rather than relying on material provided without independent follow-up or corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper trail, records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust documentary evidence (contracts, filings, records) should underpin claims; documentation increases verifiability and legal defensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sources / verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use more than one source and verify information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check facts across independent sources and documents; avoid single-source dependence and apply standard verification practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies wrongdoer or responsible party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should clearly point to who is responsible for misconduct or harmful outcomes where evidence supports such identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology disclosable
rubrics_metrics.description: Process explainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should be able to explain how they found and verified information (data methods, document trails, interviews) to support transparency and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holds power to account
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation challenges and scrutinizes those in power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to reveal abuses or lapses by officials, corporations, or institutions — especially where oversight has failed — to inform public debate and prompt accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace financial flows
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow money as a core investigative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map transactions, payments, transfers, and financial relationships to reveal hidden links and motives; use bank records, payments data, contracts, and ledgers where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify beneficial owners (vs. shell companies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish the real people behind corporate entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate ownership structures to uncover who ultimately controls assets or companies, avoiding being misled by nominee directors or shell entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference public records (tax, registration, court)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple public record types to corroborate findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine tax filings, business registrations, court records, property deeds and other official documents to validate connections and transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify offshore structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect use of offshore entities and jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for incorporation in secrecy jurisdictions, use of trusts, offshore banks, and intermediary firms that obscure ownership or movement of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect dots across jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Link evidence that spans countries and legal systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-border collaboration and analysis are needed to follow complex international financial flows and assemble a coherent narrative from dispersed records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding sources and backgrounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Locating informed sources and building context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop primary and secondary sources, build expert context, and compile background research to inform and corroborate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public records / FOI
rubrics_metrics.description: Using freedom-of-information and public records requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage FOI laws and public databases to obtain official documents; understand legal processes, exemptions, and how to craft effective requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting effective interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use best practices for preparing, questioning, and corroborating interview material; protect vulnerable sources and read legal/ethical boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep internet research
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced online investigative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OSINT tools, archival sites, social media analysis, domain and IP lookups, and web archives to uncover digital traces and corroborate leads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Following the money (training topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Skills specific to tracing financial transactions and structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should cover transaction analysis, corporate registry research, beneficial ownership, and interpreting financial documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Using data analysis to support investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply quantitative analysis, spreadsheets, databases, and visualization to spot patterns, anomalies, and quantify impacts; ensure reproducibility and clear explanation of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous verification of claims and documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically verify facts, dates, figures, and identities; document the verification trail and correct errors transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital security (for risky reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting sources, data, and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt secure communication, storage, and operational practices when reporting on sensitive topics or when sources face risk; include basic OPSEC and encryption practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations (cross-border)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working with other journalists and organizations internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate data, leads, and publication plans with partners across jurisdictions to handle transnational investigations and share resources safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial oversight and shaping of investigative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should assess evidentiary strength, legal risks, narrative clarity, verification, and appropriate presentation of findings before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrongdoing magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: How serious is the wrongdoing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scale, severity, and societal impact of the alleged misconduct; larger magnitude increases newsworthiness and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of victims
rubrics_metrics.description: How many people are affected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider breadth of harm — larger numbers of affected people heighten public significance and urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of perpetrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Influence or authority of the alleged wrongdoer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigating powerful actors (officials, large companies) is especially significant because of potential systemic impact and accountability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiddenness
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the wrongdoing concealed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hidden or deliberately obscured actions (e.g., via shell companies or secret deals) increase a story’s investigative value and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability through documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Can claims be corroborated with documents?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that can be backed by documentary evidence are stronger, more defensible, and more likely to prompt action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Local vs. transnational reach of the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transnational or multi-jurisdictional impacts can increase complexity and significance; local relevance is important for audience connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicability of the wrongdoing pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the misconduct part of a repeatable pattern?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the wrongdoing appears systemic or repeatable, the story may indicate broader problems needing reform rather than isolated incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Can exposure produce change?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether publication could lead to policy, legal, or institutional reform — stories with plausible paths to change are highly newsworthy.
